facts.fact_text: The applicant is a journalist.
The applicant is a member of Hyde Park, an unincorporated non-governmental organisation from Chișinău.
Hyde Park lobbies, inter alia, for freedom of expression and the right to peaceful assembly.
Hyde Park organised a demonstration on 8 May 2008.
The applicant decided to go on hunger strike because he was unable to trace his brother for two days.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant stood outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant positioned a placard with the inscription "Hunger strike for rights" outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
On 10 May 2008 at 10 a.m., the applicant started a silent protest outside the Government building in Chișinău's main square.
Shortly after the applicant began his silent protest on 10 May 2008, police officers approached him.
Some of the police officers who approached the applicant asked him questions.
Some of the police officers who approached the applicant filmed him.
At approximately 10.45 a.m. on 10 May 2008, the applicant was approached by two persons wearing plain clothes.
In a video filmed by the applicant, one of the two plain-clothed persons can be seen ordering the applicant to stop filming.
The applicant refused the order to stop filming and stated that he is a journalist on hunger strike.
The applicant asked the two plain-clothed persons for identification.
One of the two plain-clothed persons hit the applicant, apparently in the hand holding the camera.
One of the two plain-clothed persons threatened the applicant in rude terms with violence if he did not stop filming.
The applicant backed away while insisting that he had the right to film.
The applicant asked for the identity of the person who had hit him.
The person who hit the applicant identified himself as C.A., Commander of the Special Forces police regiment "Scut".
C.A. stated that he only wanted to talk with the applicant and insisted that the applicant stop filming.
The applicant asked C.A. why he did not want to talk with the camera on.
C.A. retorted that he was not an actor to be filmed.
The applicant asked C.A. for identification documents.
At the moment the applicant asked C.A. for identification documents, the applicant received another blow from C.A.
The applicant continued to back away while being followed by the second plain-clothed police officer.
The second plain-clothed police officer appeared to forcefully put an end to the applicant's filming.
The video filmed by the applicant resumes for several seconds showing what appears to be a police van taking the applicant away from the scene of the event.
In a video filmed by the police from another angle, the scene with the two plain-clothed police officers and the applicant can be seen from a distance.
In the police video, the camera approaches when the second plain-clothed police officer forcefully puts an end to the applicant's filming.
The second plain-clothed police officer seized the applicant by his clothes and hands.
The applicant asked the second plain-clothed police officer not to use force and insisted that he had the right to protest.
The second plain-clothed police officer retorted that by protesting the applicant was breaching the rights of other persons.
Two uniformed police officers approached and apprehended the applicant.
The two uniformed police officers took the applicant to a police van without any resistance from the applicant.
The applicant arrived at the police station at approximately 11 a.m. on 10 May 2008.
The applicant's personal effects were taken away at the police station.
The applicant was questioned for approximately two hours at the police station.
According to the applicant, he insisted on being informed of the reasons for his arrest at the police station, but to no avail.
The applicant was detained for forty-eight hours in solitary confinement in a cell without windows.
The temperature in the applicant's cell was approximately fourteen degrees centigrade.
The applicant was wearing light clothes during his detention.
There was a concrete bed in the applicant's cell, covered with wooden boards but without any bedding.
There were no sanitary facilities in the applicant's cell.
The applicant had to ask the guards to be taken to a toilet.
The guards reacted to the applicant's request to be taken to a toilet only one or two hours later, when he screamed out loud in order to be heard by their superiors.
The only water the applicant had to drink during his detention was water from the sink in the toilet.
Throughout his detention the applicant was given no food.
Nobody was allowed to visit the applicant throughout his detention.
The applicant's cell was lit with a low-energy bulb which was on continuously, with no possibility to switch it off.
After twelve hours of detention the applicant felt unwell.
The applicant's request for a doctor during his detention was ignored.
Only the next morning after the applicant felt unwell was a doctor called.
The applicant was taken by ambulance to a hospital.
The doctors at the hospital diagnosed the applicant with nephrolithiasis (kidney stones).
The doctors at the hospital diagnosed the applicant with renal colic (extremely sharp and severe pain caused by a renal stone blocking the ureter).
The doctors at the hospital decided to hospitalise the applicant.
The police officer accompanying the applicant to the hospital refused to allow the applicant to be hospitalised.
On 12 May 2008 at 11 a.m., the applicant was taken to the Buiucani District Court.
At the Buiucani District Court on 12 May 2008, the applicant learned that he had been charged with the offence of insulting police officers.
At the Buiucani District Court on 12 May 2008, the applicant learned that he had been charged with the offence of resisting arrest.
The police accused the applicant of calling them "rats", "cowards" and "Voronin's dogs" when they peacefully approached him.
At the end of the hearing on 12 May 2008, at 3 p.m., the applicant was released.
After his release, the applicant had no money or mobile telephone.
After his release, the applicant had to walk to the police station to pick up his belongings without laces on his shoes and without a belt.
At the police station, the applicant discovered that the memory of his video camera (approximately forty-five minutes of film) had been erased.
The applicant sealed his video camera in the presence of two witnesses who signed a document attesting to the sealing.
The police officer responsible for the storage of the applicant's belongings refused to sign the document attesting to the sealing of the video camera.
On the same day the applicant picked up his belongings, the applicant took his video camera to an expert.

The expert succeeded in recovering 7-10% of the contents of the erased memory of the applicant's video camera, including the images described in the video of the applicant's encounter with the plain-clothed police officers.
On 15 May 2008, the applicant lodged a criminal complaint with the Prosecutor's Office, complaining about the actions of the police officers.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had physically and verbally aggressed him.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had dispersed a peaceful protest held in accordance with the law.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had unlawfully deprived him of his liberty for forty-eight hours.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had unlawfully searched him.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had seized his possessions.
In his criminal complaint, the applicant complained that the police officers had erased the memory of his video camera.
The applicant complained that the police officers had breached several provisions of the Criminal Code.
On 26 May 2008, the criminal complaint lodged by the applicant was dismissed by the Prosecutor's Office.
The applicant appealed against the dismissal of his criminal complaint.
In his appeal, the applicant added that he had been held in inhuman and degrading conditions.
In his appeal, the applicant added that he had not been provided with appropriate medical assistance.
The video of the applicant's verbal and physical abuse in front of the Government building became the subject matter of a media scandal.
Several television stations reported on the event of the applicant's verbal and physical abuse in front of the Government building and broadcast the video footage.
On 28 May 2008, the Minister of Internal Affairs formally admonished two police officers, C.A. and V.O.
The applicant was accused by the Minister of Internal Affairs of having provoked the police officers by insulting them and resisting arrest.
The applicant was described by the Minister of Internal Affairs as someone with a systematic tendency to disturb public order.
Without any explanations, C.A. and V.O. received an admonishment for breaching several rules of police conduct, in particular unprofessional conduct, dishonesty and failure to identify themselves.
On 5 June 2008, the Buiucani District Court delivered its judgment acquitting the applicant of all charges.
The Buiucani District Court examined the videos of the applicant's encounter with the police and his arrest of 10 May 2008 before delivering its judgment.
The Buiucani District Court heard witnesses before delivering its judgment of 5 June 2008.
The Buiucani District Court found that the accusations against the applicant were false.
The Buiucani District Court found that the applicant had not insulted the police officers.
The Buiucani District Court found that the applicant had not resisted arrest.
On 15 June 2008, the Chișinău Prosecutor's Office dismissed the applicant's appeal on the ground that the police officers' behaviour did not disclose an offence.
The Chișinău Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant had insulted the police officers by calling them "rats", "cowards" and "Voronin's dogs".
The Chișinău Prosecutor's Office noted that the two police officers who had physically and verbally assaulted the applicant had been admonished for their behaviour.
The applicant lodged an appeal on points of law against the Chișinău Prosecutor's Office's decision of 15 June 2008.
On 2 July 2008, the Buiucani District Court dismissed the applicant's appeal against the Chișinău Prosecutor's Office's decision of 15 June 2008.
